records.region: Veracruz, Mexico; Maltrata–Río Blanco and lower wetland connections to the Tlalixcoyan–Alvarado lagoon complex.
records.candidate_name_role: Representative named river trunk of the selected Maltrata–Blanco–lower wetland and receiving-lagoon route; not a uniform name for every selected reach.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The two selected mainstem fragments correspond at ordinary corridor scale to the Maltrata headward approach, the extensive Río Blanco trunk through the Orizaba–Ixtaczoquitlán–Omealca corridor, and a lower southward wetland route before turning north to the Tlalixcoyan/Alvarado lagoon complex. Original state and municipal maps cover the complete selected geography. Río Blanco is a supported representative identity, while the feeder, branching wetland route and receiving waters retain their separate naming scope.
records.completion_scope: The two selected mainstem fragments correspond at ordinary corridor scale to the Maltrata headward approach, the extensive Río Blanco trunk through the Orizaba–Ixtaczoquitlán–Omealca corridor, and a lower southward wetland route before turning north to the Tlalixcoyan/Alvarado lagoon complex. Original state and municipal maps cover the complete selected geography. Río Blanco is a supported representative identity, while the feeder, branching wetland route and receiving waters retain their separate naming scope.
records.supported_name_scope: Representative named river trunk of the selected Maltrata–Blanco–lower wetland and receiving-lagoon route; not a uniform name for every selected reach.

component_scope_limits: The headward selected channel is mapped as Maltrata. The separate Encino and Acultzingo approaches are not silently renamed or substituted for the selected headward route.

Río Blanco is directly mapped along the long central river corridor. The lower selected course takes the southward wetland connection rather than simply following every northeastern branch labeled Blanco.

Tlalixcoyan and Ignacio de la Llave maps distinguish Blanco, Las Pozas, Caño Largo and named waterbodies. These source-local names are not treated as interchangeable aliases or exact vertex-by-vertex transitions.

The northward lower passage lies in the connected lagoon-margin setting mapped with Limón in the municipal source. The independent 1992 receiving-water figure distinguishes a southern Río Camarón approach from Río Blanco. No claim makes every lower channel Río Blanco, or makes Limón and Camarón formal aliases.
The terminal setting is Laguna de Tlalixcoyan within the Alvarado lagoon system. The selected geometry does not establish an extension through Boca de Alvarado to the open Gulf.

No exact bank, shoreline, mouth point, contemporary flow direction in every wetland connection, official river length or legal name boundary is established. These are not material gaps in the completed ordinary-scale representative-system review.

completion_scope.headward_scope: The selected initial eastward valley feeder and its physical confluence with the mapped Marsh Fork are visible. The mapped Marsh Fork headwaters continue outside the selected route; their name is not assigned to the initial feeder.
completion_scope.lake_scope: No large lake or reservoir interrupts the established mountain and Canning trunk. The selected coastal continuation enters a wetland landscape containing small ponds and a larger unnamed lake/outlet network. An observed lake in that corridor does not supply the missing link to the southern delta channel.
material_junctions_inspected: Unnamed western mountain feeder entering Marsh Fork Canning River
Marsh Fork entering Canning River from the west
Eastern Cache Creek and the Nanook–Ignek valley inflows along the Canning trunk
Canning delta division and western Staines-side channels
completion_scope.actual_terminal_setting: Coastal lagoon on the Beaufort Sea coast, landward of Flaxman Island and west of Brownlow Point. The rendered endpoint lies in lagoon water; the upstream terminal channel identity and its connection to the Canning/Staines delta are unresolved.
unresolved_material_connections: The selected western wetland/pond continuation between the mapped southern delta-side channels and the northern unnamed lake/outlet networks. Fine-scale original cartography does not show the needed connector.

Continuous correspondence of that western continuation to the selected coastward outlet; the nearby labeled Staines River follows a different, easterly route and cannot substitute for this missing connection.
completion_scope.gap_character: A material connector/source-correspondence gap, not absence of a name, an exact-bank requirement, or a request for precise mouth-vertex agreement. Cartographic non-depiction is not proof that no seasonal or real-world connection exists.

records.region: Northern Alaska, United States; Marsh Fork–Canning trunk and an unresolved western coastal wetland connector toward the lagoon landward of Flaxman Island.
records.candidate_name_role: Provisional representative identity of the mapped Marsh Fork–Canning trunk and its delta system. The selected western coastal continuation is not yet connected by original cartography, so this is not a completed whole-selected-route identity.
records.material_pending_reason: The selected western coastal continuation crosses a wetland and pond belt where original cartography shows southern channel ends and northern lake/outlet networks without establishing their needed connection. The nearby mapped Staines outlet follows a different route; absence of a drawn connector is not proof of physical or seasonal disconnection.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The mountainous and foothill portion of FID 2340 corresponds to an unnamed western headward feeder, Marsh Fork Canning River, and then the Canning River north through the mountains and coastal plain. Near the delta it enters the western Staines-side channel setting, but its last continuation runs through a more westerly wetland and pond corridor, separate from the continuously labeled Staines River outlet. Detailed original cartography shows southern channel ends and northern lake/outlet networks without the watercourse link needed to connect the selected coastal continuation. The selected terminal is in the coastal lagoon landward of Flaxman Island, west of Brownlow Point, rather than at the mapped main Staines mouth. The missing western connector remains material pending.
records.supported_name_scope: Provisional representative identity of the mapped Marsh Fork–Canning trunk and its delta system. The selected western coastal continuation is not yet connected by original cartography, so this is not a completed whole-selected-route identity.

component_scope_limits: The provisional Canning River candidate is supported by original maps for the connected mountainous, foothill and coastal-plain trunk. It is not a completed representative identity for the entire selected object while its western terminal connector remains unresolved.

The initial unnamed feeder, Marsh Fork Canning River, Canning River, Staines River, unnamed coastal channels, pond/lake passages and lagoon are different geographic scopes. One downstream name is not imposed on all of them.
The source gap is material and therefore is not counted as a completed river_group_name_scope_hold.
The maps do not establish official source-point coordinates, current exact banks, every seasonal channel, the cause of model/cartographic differences, or formal registry status for the model group.
FWS planning study lengths and the retained model length describe different scopes; neither is converted into a new official length for this object.
FWS planning and refuge boundary symbology is used for orientation only, without making a present legal-boundary or river-designation claim.

records.supported_name_scope: The long downstream corridor is repeatedly mapped as Housatonic River. The actual selected initial passage is Ashmere Lake, then Bennett Brook, then East Branch Housatonic River before the Pittsfield junction. Ashmere Lake, Center Pond, Woods Pond, Lake Lillinonah and Lake Zoar retain their waterbody identities; Connecticut DEEP separately identifies the lower riverine impoundment as Lake Housatonic. The estuarine islands, tidal branches and Milford-side coastal fringe are not renamed wholesale after the representative river.
records.region: Massachusetts and Connecticut, United States; Ashmere Lake–Bennett Brook–East Branch and Housatonic River to the Stratford/Milford estuarine setting.
records.candidate_name_role: Supported representative identity of the selected downstream river system. This is not a uniform scalar name for the initial lake, tributary, East Branch, reservoir passages or coastal terminal.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The selected route belongs representatively to the Housatonic River system, but starts in Ashmere Lake and follows Bennett Brook to the East Branch Housatonic River rather than starting at the usually described Muddy Pond head of the East Branch. It reaches the Housatonic mainstem at Pittsfield, continues through western Massachusetts and Connecticut, traverses the Lillinonah–Zoar–lower riverine-impoundment chain, and enters the lower Housatonic estuary. Its generalized terminal is in the Milford-side Nells Island/Cedar Beach–Milford Point shoreline complex. Original mapping distinguishes the main estuarine outlet around Nells Island from the surrounding tidal marsh and outer shoreline; no exact mouth-point or bank agreement is required or asserted.
records.completion_scope: Complete bounded original-map geographic review of both selected FIDs, including the actual initial lake/feeder, all intervening corridors and major lake/reservoir connections, material junctions and actual terminal setting. Optional regional-publication failures leave no material geographic gap and do not create an access-pending count.

The estuarine islands, tidal branches and Milford-side coastal fringe are not renamed wholesale after the representative river.

records.region: Pernambuco and Alagoas, Brazil; unnamed head feeder, Riacho do Mel–Canhoto, lower Mundaú, Lagoa Mundaú and the Atlantic-outlet corridor.
records.candidate_name_role: representative downstream river and connected-system identity only
records.geographic_disambiguation: The selected route starts on a small feeder east of Caetés in the Bastões setting, enters the Riacho do Mel/Canhoto headward corridor, continues via Canhotinho and São José da Laje to the Mundaú junction near União dos Palmares, and follows the lower Mundaú through Murici and Rio Largo into Lagoa Mundaú and its southern Atlantic-outlet setting. The original cartography and the SGB river-network diagram jointly support Rio Mundaú as the representative connected-system identity. They do not establish one uniform hydronym for all selected river, reservoir, lagoon and coastal-channel portions.
records.completion_scope: The selected route starts on a small feeder east of Caetés in the Bastões setting, enters the Riacho do Mel/Canhoto headward corridor, continues via Canhotinho and São José da Laje to the Mundaú junction near União dos Palmares, and follows the lower Mundaú through Murici and Rio Largo into Lagoa Mundaú and its southern Atlantic-outlet setting. The original cartography and the SGB river-network diagram jointly support Rio Mundaú as the representative connected-system identity. They do not establish one uniform hydronym for all selected river, reservoir, lagoon and coastal-channel portions.
records.supported_name_scope: representative downstream river and connected-system identity only

component_scope_limits: The initial small feeder in the Bastões/Caetés setting has no securely assigned local hydronym. Its candidate_name remains null; it is not equated with the report's described Riacho do Mel spring.
The Riacho do Mel and Rio Canhoto names are retained for the headward corridor; the precise boundary between their usages is not assigned.
Cajarana is a reservoir/dam name on the Canhoto headward route. It is distinct from Cajueiro on the separate upper Mundaú branch and Inhumas on the separate Inhaúma branch.

The selected northern Canhoto route is distinct from the upper Mundaú route through Correntes and Santana do Mundaú. Their confluence supports the downstream representative identity without renaming the selected headward feeder.
Lagoa Mundaú and the southern coastal channels are not assigned the scalar name Rio Mundaú. Lagoa Manguaba is a neighboring connected lagoon, not the lagoon crossed by the selected route.

The terminal correspondence is the ordinary lower-lagoon/Atlantic-outlet corridor. No precise match of the generalized endpoint to the dated cartographic inlet, sand-bar edge or bank position is asserted.

reconstruction_rule: Start from the pinned r46 cumulative index and apply later append-only deltas in verified commit order, rejecting duplicate IDs. Keep base records, scope clauses, region qualifiers and assessment histories unchanged. Apply explicit status-list changes. Subtract all recorded IDs from the exact eligible initial inventory to recover unrecorded targets; pending IDs remain recorded but are not completed source reviews.
publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Follow the actual continental order: Americas, Asia, Africa, Europe, then other, with all rivers before lakes. Preserve original queue IDs and ranks for continuity; apply documented geographic deferrals without counting them as name research, and place deferred objects into their corrected later phase by length-descending, stable-ID order. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated.
